Background: Sulphur Bank Mercury Mine (SBMM) is a 160-acre former cinnabar mercury mining site located on the eastern shore of the Oaks Arm of Clear Lake, approximately 70 miles northwest of Sacramento in Lake County, California. The mine operated from 1865 to 1957, utilizing both underground and open pit mining technologies. SBMM consists of mine tailings and waste rock and a flooded open pit mine (the Herman Impoundment). Approximately two million cubic yards of waste rock and low-grade ore remain onsite and contain high levels of mercury, arsenic and antimony. The Herman Impoundment is filled with water to a depth of 90 feet and is located approximately 750 feet east of Clear Lake, which is separated from the impoundment by an earthen dam composed of waste rock material and in-place bedrock. SBMM was placed on the Superfund National Priorities List (NPL) in August 1990 due to the impact of site contamination on the residents near the mine and wildlife in the vicinity of Clear Lake. The SBMM site results in uncontrolled exposure to site-related contaminants for multiple user groups. This exposure results in unacceptable risk greatly exceeding EPA’s risk management range.
